title: Grafana 9.4 fails to load through a Cloudflare Tunnel
body: I am running a simple Grafana instance in Docker on Ubuntu 22.04 behind a Cloudflare Tunnel. After upgrading Grafana from 9.3 to 9.4, it no longer loads through Cloudflare and shows: "If you're seeing this Grafana has failed to load its application files". It still loads internally through the direct IP and port, and reverting the image to 9.3 makes it work again. I want to understand what changed and whether Grafana or Cloudflare needs to be reconfigured.

symptoms_visible: Grafana 9.4 shows "If you're seeing this Grafana has failed to load its application files" when I access it through Cloudflare.
The same instance loads through its direct internal IP and port, and reverting the image to Grafana 9.3 makes it load through Cloudflare again.
N0.label: N0 Grafana 9.4 fails through Cloudflare

symptoms_visible: The application-files error occurs through Cloudflare on multiple Grafana 9.4 builds and machines, while rolling back to 9.3.6 restores access.
N1.label: N1 upgrade regression confirmed by affected users

symptoms_visible: Grafana still shows the application-files error after I set the Cloudflare page rule to bypass caching and disable performance, then purged the Cloudflare and browser caches multiple times.
N2_x.label: N2_x cache-bypass workaround aftermath

symptoms_visible: With Cloudflare JavaScript Auto Minify enabled, Grafana fails to load; after I disable that option and clear the Cloudflare and browser caches, Grafana 9.4.3 loads normally through Cloudflare.
N3.label: N3 Cloudflare optimization interaction isolated

symptoms_visible: Grafana loads normally through the Cloudflare Tunnel after JavaScript Auto Minify is disabled and the cached application files are cleared.
N_terminal.label: terminal Grafana loads through Cloudflare

question_patterns: Does this happen on more than one Grafana 9.4 build or machine?
Can anyone else reproduce the failure after upgrading to the 9.4 series?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. I have seen it with the 9.4.0 beta and 9.4.1 on multiple machines, and other affected installations report the same failure after moving to 9.4.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: No, it only happens on this one machine, and a fresh Grafana 9.4 container works through the same tunnel.
I reproduce it on 9.4.1 and 9.4.2 rather than the beta, with the same error.

question_patterns: Which exact older image works when you roll back?
Does rolling back restore access without changing the Cloudflare tunnel?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Rolling back to 9.3.6 restores access through the same Cloudflare setup.

edges.comment: Reports from several affected users are folded into one simulated user side. They establish that the behavior follows the Grafana 9.4 upgrade rather than one host.

solution.intent: Work around the failure using a Cloudflare page rule that bypasses caching and disables performance features, followed by Cloudflare and browser cache purges.
solution.concrete_example: Add a Cloudflare page rule with Cache Level set to Bypass and Disable Performance, purge the Cloudflare cache, then hard-refresh or clear the browser's site data.

edges.comment: This workaround helped some participants but was explicitly falsified by another affected user on Grafana 9.4.2 after repeated Cloudflare and browser purges. It is therefore not a reliable final fix.

question_patterns: Can you isolate which Cloudflare Speed or Optimization feature changes the result?
Please test the Cloudflare optimization options individually and report which setting affects whether Grafana loads.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Disabling JavaScript under Speed > Optimization > Auto Minify makes Grafana load. With JavaScript Auto Minify enabled, it breaks again. After disabling it, I also need to purge Cloudflare and clear the Grafana site's browser data.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: None of the Cloudflare optimization settings changes the failure; it still happens even when all content transformations are disabled.
The same setting controls the result, but I had to restart the browser after clearing its site data.

question_patterns: Do the browser tools identify a particular application file that differs or fails through Cloudflare?
Which JavaScript resource is associated with the loading failure?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The file associated with the failure is `/public/build/512.6743f01f38a1921b4ef9.js`. Clearing that specific file from Cloudflare's cache also mattered for another affected installation.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: No JavaScript bundle fails; the request is instead rejected by the tunnel before any application files are returned.

edges.comment: Handler-directed configuration isolation is modeled as a measurement even though the successful toggle also serves as the workaround. Multiple affected users are folded into the user side.

solution.intent: Stop Cloudflare from rewriting Grafana's already-minified JavaScript: leave JavaScript Auto Minify disabled for the Grafana site, purge the transformed files from Cloudflare and the browser, then verify that Grafana loads through the tunnel.
solution.concrete_example: In Cloudflare, open Speed > Optimization > Auto Minify and turn off JavaScript for the Grafana site. Perform a complete Cloudflare purge, clear the Grafana site's browser data or restart the browser, and reload through the tunnel. The issue is caused by Cloudflare modifying Grafana's already-minified vendor JavaScript, not by the tunnel proxying requests to Grafana.
solution.inference_hint: The final maintainer diagnosis is that Grafana's valid, already-minified vendor chunk conflicts with Cloudflare Auto Minify, an unsupported source-rewriting feature that may strip or transform characters based on assumptions that do not hold for newer or pre-minified JavaScript. The users supplied the toggle result and affected file; interpreting that evidence as a Cloudflare transformation conflict is engineer-side inference.

edges.comment: Final accepted resolution: disable Cloudflare JavaScript Auto Minify and remove its cached transformed assets. Grafana maintainers did not treat Cloudflare Auto Minify as an officially supported deployment feature.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause: Cloudflare JavaScript Auto Minify rewrites an already-minified Grafana 9.4 vendor bundle and produces content that prevents Grafana's application files from loading; the Cloudflare Tunnel itself is not the failing component.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the collected evidence: direct-origin access works, older Grafana images work through the same tunnel, the failure follows 9.4 builds, and toggling Cloudflare's JavaScript optimization controls the result.
The final recommendation must disable JavaScript Auto Minify for the Grafana site and purge both Cloudflare's cached transformed files and the browser's cached site data.
Must not present the Cache Level: Bypass and Disable Performance page rule alone as a reliable fix, because it remained broken for an affected user even after repeated purges.
Must ask the user to verify that Grafana loads through Cloudflare after applying the configuration change and clearing caches before declaring the issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Infrastructure-focused operator rather than an application developer; comfortable deploying Docker images, configuring Cloudflare Tunnel and dashboard settings, changing versions, and clearing layered caches.
persona_hint.communication_style: Direct and practical; emphasizes reproducible upgrade behavior, asks for the relevant breaking change, follows precise configuration steps, and reports an ordered verification procedure.
